text:
incident-bot: SEVINCIDENT: elevated 5xx + timeouts on /v1/generate across multiple regions. 5m 5xx rate 11.8% (baseline ~0.4%). Paging oncall (Jamie) and SRE. Graphs: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/1789456789 :rotating_light:

Jamie (oncall): saw it, joining. @Maya can you take SRE lead? tagging runtime + ml to eyeball changes.

Maya (sre): on it. quick question — is this single-region or multi-region? any customer reports?

Kate (support): we have realtime tickets from AcmeCorp and BetaCo about timeouts and 502s starting ~09:03 UTC. Example error from Acme: "gateway timeout after 30s".

Alex (eng-runtime): throwing up logs. I'm seeing repeated KV prefix cache errors around the same time:
```
2026-05-12T09:02:41Z runtime ERROR kv_prefix_cache: shard=42 corrupt_entry detected checksum mismatch, key_prefix=\"usr:acme:session:abc123\"
2026-05-12T09:02:41Z runtime WARN request 0x7fb2 -> fallback path triggered, reason=kv_prefix_cache_corrupt
2026-05-12T09:02:43Z router ERROR 5xx from worker 10.2.4.9: read timeout
```

Lee (eng-ml): nothing changed on model side from our deployments yesterday. however we did flip a cache tuning feature yesterday afternoon (lru_eviction_ratio -> 0.25) in the runtime config to test throughput. commit: 3f9a7b2. Could be related.

Maya (sre): good call. if the prefix cache is returning corruption it can surface as 5xx/gateway errors when workers hit a panic path. Need scope: which shards/pools are noisy and how many requests hit fallback.

Alex (eng-runtime): running query: `SELECT count(*) FROM request_metrics WHERE error_type LIKE '%kv_prefix%' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes' GROUP BY worker_pool;`
Results: pool-a: 1.3k hits, pool-b: 870 hits, pool-c: 0. Polling more.

Jamie (oncall): immediate mitigations? do we have a toggle to bypass prefix cache quickly?

Alex (eng-runtime): yes, we have an admin gate: POST /admin/runtime/flags {"bypass_prefix_cache": true}. Gateway: http://runtime-admin.internal:8080/flags. I can flip but prefer SRE to advise.

Maya (sre): do it. Bypass first to stop corrupt entries from causing panics. Then we can decide clear vs targeted purge. Also ramp instances so fallback path capacity doesn't saturate.

Alex (eng-runtime): executing now:
```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}' \
  -d '{"bypass_prefix_cache":true}' \
  http://runtime-admin.internal:8080/admin/runtime/flags
```

Alex (eng-runtime): response: 200 OK {"bypass_prefix_cache":true} :white_check_mark:

Maya (sre): good. immediate effect?

incident-bot: Metric update: 5xx rate dropped to 3.9% within 90s of flag flip. Latency tail still elevated.

Jamie (oncall): routing load to fallback path increased, some workers showing higher CPU. Can we autoscale or route a subset of traffic to dedicated capacity?

Lee (eng-ml): we can route heavy customers to a dedicated variant pinned to uncached model for a short window. Need list of customer ids.

Kate (support): AcmeCorp customer ID 10023, BetaCo 10089. They're asking for ETA.

Maya (sre): I'll trigger a temporary scale-up on pool-a (increase desired to +25%) and add more workers to pool-b. Also starting targeted purge command for suspected shards (42,43,49). Alex pls run purge with debug on.

Alex (eng-runtime): running purge: 
```
POST http://runtime-admin.internal:8080/admin/cache/purge
Body: {"shards": [42,43,49], "mode": "validate_and_purge"}
```

Alex (eng-runtime): purge response: 202 Accepted. purge jobs queued: job_id=purge-20260512-09-07.

Maya (sre): monitoring job logs. If purge fails we have to fallback to full restart of affected workers which will be noisy.

incident-bot: Purge job purge-20260512-09-07 status=completed. details: 3 shards validated, corrupt entries removed, 2.1k keys cleared.

Maya (sre): confirmed from logs: checksums for those shards corrected after purge. I'm seeing error reduction to ~1.1% 5xx.

Jamie (oncall): great. can we re-enable prefix cache in safe mode (read-only warming) or do we wait for a full rollout?

Alex (eng-runtime): safe mode available: set `bypass_prefix_cache=false` + `prefix_cache_read_only=true` + warmers disabled. I'll stage it to pool-c first.

Alex (eng-runtime): staging safe-mode flip to pool-c now.

Alex (eng-runtime): pool-c flip result: 200 OK. No regressions observed in 2 minutes.

incident-bot: Metrics update: 5xx rate steady at 0.9% last 5m, latency p95 back to baseline for most pools, small tail at p99 for pool-a.

Ravi (product): preparing customer comms. Draft: "We're investigating elevated errors earlier today affecting some requests to /v1/generate. Issue traced to a runtime cache inconsistency which we've mitigated. If you continue to see errors please reply to this thread or open a ticket." Want to add status link.

Kate (support): please include AcmeCorp and BetaCo in targeted outreach now.

Maya (sre): summary and next steps:
- Immediate mitigation: bypass_prefix_cache flipped -> drop in 5xx
- Purge corrupt shards 42/43/49 completed
- Safe-mode reenabled on pool-c and monitoring for 30m
- Scale-up applied to pool-a/pool-b to absorb fallback load

Action items:
- eng-runtime (Alex): run full diagnostic on eviction logic and validate LRU ratio config (owner: Alex, due: +24h)
- eng-ml (Lee): confirm whether model traffic patterns could have amplified cache churn (owner: Lee, due: +24h)
- sre (Maya): produce postmortem with timeline, root cause, remediation and follow-ups (owner: Maya, due: 48h)
- product/support (Ravi/Kate): customer notifications + outreach (owner: Ravi/Kate, due: asap)

Jamie (oncall): I'll stay on for handoff for 30m and then pass to Maya for the follow-up. If anything spikes ping me directly. :thumbsup:

Maya (sre): noted. marking follow-up tasks. Postmortem required.

incident-bot: Incident incident-1789456789 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Escalation tickets created: INC-20260512-1789456789.

Alex (eng-runtime): quick note — found an edge-case in prefix hash compaction where zero-length prefixes could collide after GC, which apparently created the corrupt checksum. will include patch in PR 7b9c4.

Lee (eng-ml): adding evals to simulate churn-heavy traffic tomorrow to verify cache stability.

Ravi (product): sending customer notes now.

Kate (support): AcmeCorp confirmed decreased errors after our fix. BetaCo still seeing occasional 502s — investigating with them now.

Maya (sre): keep this thread updated. we will reconvene if 5xx > 2% for 10m. otherwise we'll move to postmortem and close after actions are tracked.

Jamie (oncall): thanks team. good job moving fast. :clap:
